title: Generating two-mechanical mode entangled cat states, and steady-state entanglement, in cavity optomechanics in the presence of dissipation
abstract: We investigate a dissipation-engineering approach to produce a phase-dependent collective-mode Schrödinger cat state involving two modes. Our model features a single cavity mode that interacts with two spectrally identical mechanical oscillators. Both oscillators are coupled through a phase-dependent hopping interaction. We demonstrate that by adjusting the phase of the phonon-hopping interaction, one can control the bipartite entanglement of the phase-dependent two-mode cat state during its generation. Additionally, our study reveals that phonon interactions act as a tunable parameter, enabling the manipulation of steady-state entanglement between the bare mechanical modes, even in the presence of environmental effects and thermal excitations. Our scheme provides a feasible approach for the phase-dependent multi mode non-Gaussian states preparation.
summary: The paper demonstrates a method to generate highly entangled two-mode Schrödinger cat states in cavity optomechanics by carefully controlling the system's dissipation. By tuning the phase of an interaction term ($	heta$), researchers can maximize bipartite entanglement between mechanical modes, proving that engineered environmental coupling is a powerful tool for quantum state preparation.
main_problem: The study investigates generating two-mechanical mode entangled Schrödinger cat states (SCS) and characterizing steady-state entanglement in a cavity optomechanical system subject to environmental dissipation.
main_result: The phase of the phonon-hopping interaction ($	heta$) can be tuned to control bipartite entanglement, achieving maximum entanglement at intermediate phases like $	heta=\pi/2$, even when considering thermal excitations.
method: The analysis involves deriving an effective master equation for the mechanical modes via adiabatic elimination of the cavity field and quantifying entanglement using logarithmic negativity ($\mathcal{E}_N$).
model_or_system: The system is a hybrid cavity optomechanical platform with one cavity mode coupled to two spectrally identical, interacting mechanical oscillators. The dynamics are governed by a master equation incorporating damping from both the cavity and mechanical baths.
key_observables: Bipartite entanglement (quantified by logarithmic negativity $\mathcal{E}_N$), Schrödinger cat state formation, and steady-state coherence ($c(t)$).
important_parameters: The phase of the phonon-hopping interaction ($	heta$), mechanical damping rates ($\Gamma$), cavity decay rate ($\gamma_a$), and coupling strengths ($g_0$).
main_assumptions: Adiabatic elimination of the fast-decaying cavity mode is used, and some analytical approximations rely on weak phonon exchange interactions ($\chi \ll \Gamma_2$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the system components (Fig. 1), show bipartite entanglement vs. $	heta$ (maximized at $\pi/2$), and demonstrate temporal evolution of fidelity $F(t)$ confirming analytical accuracy limits.
paper_structure: The paper models the full Hamiltonian, derives a reduced master equation for mechanical modes using adiabatic elimination, analyzes the system in collective eigenmode bases ($	ext{D}\pm$), and finally calculates entanglement measures to show phase-dependent control over quantum states.
why_interesting: This work exemplifies advanced reservoir engineering by showing how controlled dissipation can stabilize non-Gaussian entangled states (cat states) in mechanical oscillators, a key area for quantum sensing and computation using macroscopic quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. A schematic diagram of a cavity optomechanical sys- tem consists of a single cavity and two mechanical modes. The radiation pressure and phonon-hopping interactions are shown in black and red arrows, respectively. Single photon optomechanical coupling is g0, and the phonon-phonon inter- action is characterized by χ and θ. Cavity is driven by the pump field of amplitude and phase εp and ωp. Along with that, a coherent drive of amplitude εd and frequency ωd is also applied to the cavity.

FIG. 2. The central panel shows evolution of bipartite entanglement between the collective modes. The panels a(b) and c(d) depict the Wigner function of the bright(dark) mode when θ = 0 and π/2 at normalized time Γ2t = 0.5, respectively. We consider the degenerate mechanical modes with resonance frequency ωm/2π = 15 MHz and decay rate Γ/2π = 15 Hz, respectively. Thermal occupancy of each mechanical mode nb = 0. The exchange interaction between the two mechanical modes is characterized by the interaction amplitude χ/Γ2 = 10−2. The other parameters are ∆= −2ωm, γa/2π = 100 kHz, g0/2π = 1 MHz, ¯α = 0.02 and β = 1.6.

FIG. 3. Temporal evolution of the conditional state of the bright mode. The phonon hopping interaction strength is charac- terized by χ/Γ2 = 0.01 and ϕ = π/2. All the other parameters are same as in Fig. 2.

FIG. 4. Steady-state bipartite entanglement between the col- lective modes as a function of χ and θ, when thermal excita- tion of each mechanical mode is 0.5. Red dashed line suggest θ = π/2. All the other parameters are the same as Fig. 2.

FIG. 5. Steady-state bipartite entanglement between the bare mechanical modes as a function of χ and θ, when thermal excitation of each mechanical mode is 0.5. Red dashed line suggest θ = π/2. All the other parameters are the same as Fig. 2.
